defects.quote: NO_POLICY because no resource policy or required capacity is configured
defects.why: NO_POLICY does not establish which condition caused it, and required capacity does not determine a resource verdict.

defects.quote: configure an explicit resource policy (e.g., LOWER_BOUND/UPPER_BOUND/BOUNDED)
defects.why: Those are capacity bound types, not resource policy rules an operator can configure.

defects.quote: only a configured policy or required capacity yields PASS or FAIL for resources
defects.why: Required capacity alone cannot produce a PASS or FAIL resource verdict.

notes: The coverage and clock checks are useful, but the resource policy advice could misdirect configuration.

defects.quote: the errors profile query against opensearch failed with SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR after 2 retries, so the error-rate policy check ... may not cover the full run
defects.why: The policy check covers the shorter evaluation window; the failed OpenSearch query is not shown to cause that coverage.

defects.quote: the 1,315-sample difference plus dropped leading/trailing cells is consistent with partial acquisition
defects.why: The difference compares a whole-run count with a policy-window denominator and does not indicate missing acquisition.

defects.quote: compare error counts for the full run window ... to confirm the zero-error result covers samples outside the policy-check window
defects.why: OpenSearch error counts cannot confirm coverage of the same JMeter samples without event linkage.
The aggregates do not give the number of samples tied at each maximum.

notes: Several operator checks are useful, but the response mislinks source failure and counts to policy coverage.
